body:
A part started in the background now takes its step from its own worktree, not from the environment it inherited: its saves carry its own name even if it started inside a process made for another part. If the two disagree, the part is told once and keeps working as its own step. The live two-launch probe still has to be run on your laptop: this container refused to start background sessions.

### What changed
- `kit.py launch` writes `.kit/run/step` (the post id) in the part's worktree before it runs `claude --bg`. `resume --role part --post X` writes it too, since the prompt names the right step even when the environment does not.
- One reading of "which step is this worktree": `own_step` in `kit/landing.py`. Order: `.kit/run/step`, then the post `resume --role part` marked for this branch, then (when the caller knows it) the post whose branch this is, and KIT_POST only when none of those exists or it agrees.
- Users of it: `kit.py checkpoint` (the commit label, which was `KIT_POST or branch`), `_my_post`, the save hook's "is this a part's branch", `kit_task_train.part_post`, `kit_activity`. Without `.kit/landing.py` each falls back to KIT_POST as before.
- When KIT_POST names another step: a single STEP note ("this session's environment names step M1, but this worktree is step CL44: working as CL44, its saves are labelled CL44"), recorded in `.kit/run/step-disagree.json` so it is said once per pair.

### Probe (step 1, for the laptop)
In two scratch folders a and b that Claude Code trusts, each with a `.claude/settings.json` SessionStart hook `echo "KIT_POST=$KIT_POST" >> seen.txt`, run one right after the other:
`KIT_POST=POST-A claude --bg -n probe-a --model haiku "Reply ok."` in a, then `KIT_POST=POST-B claude --bg -n probe-b ...` in b; then read a/seen.txt and b/seen.txt. A warm spare shows POST-A in b (or nothing).

### Board copy
The first pull read only this post. The reconcile it asked for then wanted to write 372 documents (the whole board, as if the Artifact had none of them): not sent, kept outside the repo; reconcile belongs to a full pull.

task:
A part launched with `claude --bg` knows its own step. CL44's part was started while M1's part had just been launched, and its environment named M1's post (KIT_POST): its automatic save commits were labelled with M1's name. A likely cause: `claude --bg` hands the work to a warm spare process made earlier, whose environment is not the one the launch passed (the launch sets KIT_POST, KIT_ROLE and the task list id in its subprocess environment).

1. Confirm the cause: launch two parts one after the other and read each session's KIT_POST.
2. A part's step never rests on the environment alone: the launch records the worktree's step (`.kit/run/step` in the worktree, or the branch's post), and the hooks read that first; KIT_POST only when it agrees.
3. When the two disagree, the hooks say so once, never label commits with the other step.
title: A part launched in the background knows its own step
verdict: Yes for the fix: the launch writes the step into the worktree before the session starts, saves and hooks read it first, and a disagreeing environment is said once; the cause itself is not yet confirmed live.
